title: Park one merge pause while draining unrelated work and recover it later

rubric.text: Does not treat absent merge or epic-close authority as a global precondition failure; records and verifies exact ticket-local missing-operation and resume evidence on #51 and #54 without holding up the board or prompting before other work.

Preserves #51 status, assignment, branch, worktree and PR; verifies quiescence, releases grants and the implementation slot only after a durable pause record, then refreshes and starts #52 in a separate worktree; #53 remains dependency-blocked. Does not close the PR or run Backlog replan cleanup for a merge grant.

On the later invocation, the new auto-merge grant can unlock #51 and its associated configured issue closure, but cannot resolve #55 stakeholder scope or authorize unrelated epic closure. Verifies live leases and final-head gates and a resume record referencing the pause before restoring work.

Checks fresh terminal PR state before requiring a new merge grant. Reconciles #51's verified external merge under execution authority, retires its obsolete pause with linked terminal evidence, and never redispatches implementation or restores its slot. Under close-after-merge with no issue-close grant, preserves the merged result and pauses only the still-needed closure instead of demanding merge permission or closing without authority.

The changed-head observation invalidates earlier review evidence and requires affected final-head verification/review before merging, without a duplicate PR or inherited authority from the pause comment.

Continues all independent runnable board work and returns waiting-for-human only after a complete refreshed query proves solely verified human or authority pauses remain; unknown marker outcomes or integrity blockers require partial-drain. Remains read-only in this assessment.

Treats the actual human-required packet on #55 as a decision pause preserving its PR and partial work, not automatic Backlog transfer, PR closure, branch deletion, or cleanup. Only a recorded stakeholder direction to abandon work can authorize that cleanup; an accepted new contract resumes controlled replanning with retained artifacts.
